name: Malluch
overview: Malluch was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically connected to the Merarite lineage descending from Merari, son of Levi. He is identified uniquely as the son of Hashabiah, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:44. His association with the Levitical family highlights his role within the priestly or temple service divisions of ancient Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Malluch means 'counselor' or 'king,' reflecting a title of authority or guidance. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries significant meaning within the Hebrew context, emphasizing leadership qualities.
familyAndRelationships: Malluch is explicitly noted as the son of Hashabiah according to 1 Chronicles 6:45. There is an inferred relationship suggesting Abdi as his father, based on 1 Chronicles 6:44. Scripture thus records Malluch’s immediate family connections within the Levitical line, underscoring his place in the genealogical record.
scriptureSignificance: Malluch’s significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, specifically among the Merarites, who were responsible for particular duties in the service of the tabernacle. His identification as the son of Hashabiah situates him within the priestly tribe that served God’s covenant community, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical service and heritage. Though not a central figure in narrative events, Malluch’s mention preserves the detailed record of God’s appointed servants and their families.
